title: Fall Armyworm in Corn: How to Spot, Scout and Manage It
metaTitle: Fall Armyworm: Signs, Scouting and Control in Corn
metaDescription: Fall armyworm reached the Philippines in 2019 and has spread to many regions. Learn to spot it early, scout the whorl and manage it with IPM.
excerpt: The fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) is a caterpillar that chews corn from the seedling stage to the ear. The first Philippine report came in June 2019, from Piat, Cagayan. By October 2019 it had reached 83 towns and cities in 15 regions. This guide shows how to recognize it, scout your field, and combine natural enemies with the right insecticides.

blocks.text:
The fall armyworm is the larva of a night flying moth native to the Americas. It prefers corn, but it also feeds on rice, sorghum, sugarcane and some vegetables.

In the Philippines, the first suspected case came from a cornfield in Piat, Cagayan on June 20, 2019. Scientists at UPLB confirmed the species by DNA barcoding. Four months later the pest was in 83 towns and cities across 15 regions, according to the country report filed with the IPPC.

The Bureau of Plant Industry now leads a National Fall Armyworm Action Plan. It covers monitoring with pheromone traps, biological control, farmer training and research.

items: **Eggs.** Masses of about 120 to 200 eggs on the underside of lower leaves, covered with scales from the moth.
**Young larvae.** Small and greenish, feeding in groups. They scrape the leaf surface so it looks like a thin window.
**Older larvae.** Brown to dark, up to 4 or 5 cm long, with three pale lines along the back and dark spots that carry short spines.
**The two marks that settle it.** An upside down Y on the head, and four black dots in a square on the last segment of the body.
**Damage.** Ragged holes in whorl leaves, eaten edges, and wet frass that looks like sawdust in the whorl. Later, larvae bore into the ears.

blocks.text:
Damage builds fastest at the whorl stage. The larvae hide deep in the funnel of young leaves and eat them before they open. On seedlings, they can also cut the plant at the base.

After that, they move to the tassels and bore into the ears. The USDA 2024 report on the Philippines says fall armyworm has severely hurt corn through stunting and damage to tassels and kernels, which cuts grain quality and yield.

Good control pays. In a DA Cagayan Valley IPM demonstration reported in May 2025, the IPM plot yielded 7,781 kg per hectare in the dry season. The usual farmer practice next to it yielded 2,417 kg.

items.title: Walk a W
items.text: Walk the field in a W pattern and stop at five points. At each stop, check 10 plants in a row, for 50 plants in all.

items.title: Count infested plants
items.text: Count plants with fresh whorl damage or live larvae. Then multiply by two to get the percent of plants infested.

items.title: Check for eggs
items.text: Turn over lower leaves and crush any egg masses you find by hand.

items.title: Repeat every week
items.text: Scout at least once a week from emergence to tasseling, and more often when your pheromone trap starts catching moths.

items.title: Decide
items.text: In the DA Cagayan Valley IPM protocol, farmers used chemical insecticides only when infestation passed 10 percent.

items: Plant at the same time as your neighbors, and avoid planting next to older corn that already carries larvae.
Keep the field and borders free of weeds, and follow balanced fertilization.
Crush egg masses and young larvae by hand while you scout.
Rotate crops when you can, and plow under infested stubble after harvest.

blocks.text:
The DA Cagayan Valley IPM protocol starts biological control early. Earwigs (Euborellia) go out at about 10,000 per hectare within five days after planting. Trichogramma chilonis cards follow at 50 per hectare between days 5 and 10. After that, sprays of Metarhizium and Beauveria, two fungi that infect caterpillars, come at set intervals.

Birds, ants, beetles and wild earwigs also eat larvae. So avoid broad spectrum sprays early in the season that would kill them too.
Pick by active ingredient and group, not by brand, and rotate groups between sprays to slow resistance. Aim the spray into the whorl, where the larvae hide, and hit them while they are small.

blocks.text:
Note the last two rows. The insecticide Karate and the pyrethroid in Cymbush are familiar names at the agrivet store. But their Syngenta Philippines labels do not list fall armyworm on corn, and the Pacific pests fact sheet notes that the moth reached Africa already resistant to pyrethroids, among other insecticides. Ask your technician whether resistance is a problem in your area.

So choose a product whose FPA registered label names this pest on corn, and follow its rate and harvest interval. Read more in our guide to [Karate, Cymbush and Selecron](/blog/karate-cymbush-selecron-insecticides).

blocks.title: Follow the label and the FPA registration
blocks.text: Only spray products registered with the [Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority](/blog/fertilizer-and-pesticide-authority) for your crop and pest. The label gives the rate, the interval between sprays and the days to wait before harvest. Wear protective gear, and keep children and animals away from treated rows.
Fall armyworm or Asian corn borer?

Both caterpillars attack the whorl, so farmers often mix them up. The [Asian corn borer](/problems/asian-corn-borer) larva is creamy to pinkish with dark spots, and it tunnels into the stalk. The FAW larva is darker, carries the upside down Y and the four dots, and feeds in the whorl without boring the stem, as the ASEAN FAW Action program notes. Name the pest first, because Trichogramma timing and labels differ between the two.

items.q: When did fall armyworm reach the Philippines?
items.a: The first suspected case came from Piat, Cagayan on June 20, 2019. UPLB confirmed it by DNA barcoding, and by October 2019 it was in 15 regions.

items.q: Does Bt corn stop fall armyworm?
items.a: Do not count on it. Bt corn in the Philippines targets mainly the Asiatic corn borer, and the USDA 2024 report notes that seed companies are still researching biotech corn that resists it. Keep scouting Bt fields too.

items.q: Can I use Karate or Cymbush on fall armyworm?
items.a: Their Syngenta Philippines labels list armyworms on rice, not this pest on corn. Choose a product whose label names it on corn.

items.q: Does fall armyworm attack rice too?
items.a: It can. The Pacific pests fact sheet lists rice among its hosts, and one strain prefers rice and pasture grasses. Watch for it and see our guide to [rice insects](/problems/rice-insects).
